# compensation_entries

Compensation entries records in Operations Desk. Product articles define their operational scope.

Read this collection using `search_records(resource="compensation_entries", filters={}, cursor=0, limit=20)` or `get_record(resource="compensation_entries", record_id="<returned id>")`.

**Filters:** exact scalar equality; in, contains, gte and lte operator objects on supported top-level fields. See DB-query-syntax for type and null behavior.

Search returns selected summary fields, so omission from a summary is not proof of absence from the complete record. Read detail before interpreting an optional field. Fields depend on the record type and processing stage; null and absent fields are not zero amounts. Types below describe public record shapes, rather than mandatory properties on every row.

## Fields

| Field | Observed public types | Search use | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount_minor` | integer | Top-level filter | Amount in integer minor currency units. Whether it denotes an instruction, liability or posted movement depends on this record type. |
| `business_area` | string | Top-level filter | Business area: public attribute of this record type. The associated service article defines its operational use. |
| `case_id` | string | Top-level filter | Case id: opaque identifier reference. Its target depends on the containing record/operation; do not infer a collection merely by pluralizing the field name. Explicit joins are listed separately. |
| `commercial_reference` | string | Top-level filter | Reference supplied by a commercial source; use the source and period when matching evidence. |
| `dispute_id` | string | Top-level filter | Dispute id: opaque identifier reference. Its target depends on the containing record/operation; do not infer a collection merely by pluralizing the field name. Explicit joins are listed separately. |
| `id` | string | Top-level filter | Opaque record key used by get_record; obtain it from returned records or explicit references. It is not an amount, date or proof of business identity. |
| `kind` | string | Top-level filter | Record or service type. Fields and meanings can differ between kinds. Public values represented here: `CARD_NETWORK`, `DISPUTE`, `MERCHANT`. This list describes the documented records, not an input-validation enum. |
| `published_status_updates` | array | Top-level filter | Published status updates: list of the named business attributes or references; inspect all entries relevant to the record. |
| `received_minute` | integer | Top-level filter | Received minute: logical minute or duration, as indicated by the field name; compare with get_clock and the applicable event/validity terms. |
| `scope` | string | Top-level filter | Access namespace for the record. It is not a customer name or a universal case_id. |
| `shipment_reference` | string | Top-level filter | Shipment reference: commercial reference, which may differ from the storage id. Match using the documented reference field and business context. |
| `status` | string | Top-level filter | Current state of this particular object. A proposal or submission state is distinct from a posted payment or completed review. Public values represented here: `FAILED`, `PROMISED`, `PROVISIONAL`, `SETTLED`. This list describes the documented records, not an input-validation enum. |
